newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt-bound German steelworkers lay down tools.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt-bound German steelworkers lay down tools.

text.p: Steelworkers at Thyssen AG and the Krupp group downed tools early on Tuesday as around 150 buses lined up outside Ruhr Valley factories to carry thousands to a mass protest in Frankfurt.

Thyssen work council representatives confirmed that a demonstration expected to involve up to 30,000 protestors was still due to go ahead in the German financial capital despite Monday's late announcement by Krupp that it had called off its hostile takeover bid for Thyssen.
Instead, the two companies are planning to set up a joint steel venture and explore other areas of cooperation, a move which workers and union leaders still fear could put thousands of jobs at risk.
Steel production at Krupp in Dortmund and at Thyssen in Duisburg was halted early on Tuesday, with production running at minimum capacity overnight, the work council representatives said.

The steelworkers, who fear a takeover would cost at least 7,000 jobs at the two companies, look set to paralyse traffic in Frankfurt by marching to the banking district and staging a rally just a stone's throw away from the twin-towered headquarters of Deutsche Bank AG.
Police said on Monday they did not expect any violence but would set up a security cordon outside the building to prevent workers gaining entry.
The rally is being organised by engineering union IG Metall and will take place at midday. IG Metall's combative president Klaus Zwickel will be among the speakers.

Deutsche, Dresdner Bank AG and U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs advised Krupp in its bid for Thyssen. Those three banks together with other banks were also due to provide Krupp with funding for the takeover.

They had been accused by politicians and union leaders of joining a corporate raid that goes against the grain of Germany's consensus culture and which could cause heavy job losses at a time of record postwar unemployment.
